intro.line1: Earth is always making a sound.
intro.l1: Every day, Earth experiences countless changes around us.
intro.l2: Temperatures rise and fall, forests are affected, and storms begin to form.
intro.l3: With Earth Listens, you can discover these phenomena through sounds generated from real scientific data.
intro.l4: Each phenomenon has its own unique sound, helping you better understand what's happening on our planet.
intro.l5: Discover the world not just with your eyes, but with your ears.
intro.l6: Earth Listens – Listen to the Earth's story.
intro.l7: Open the application and start your journey!

story.c1title: Earth is always making a sound.
story.c1body: Before the pictures, there is a tone. A slow drone is the first sample of carbon dioxide, held quietly so you can find the room.
story.c2body: The Earth Information Center draws the planet as frames. This sample frame is labelled SAMPLE. The real frames plug in later, from the same contract.
story.c3body: A chart that only exists as colour leaves people out. The counts behind this sentence are not filled in yet. [citation needed: Basmala]
story.c4body: Where, how much, how strong, how fast, what. Each question is a separate part of the sound, and the order of the notes follows the data.
story.c5body: The sample temperature series runs from 1880 to 2025. Scrub a year. The pitch is the value. Nothing here is a forecast.
story.c6body: Start the jukebox, switch to audio-first, walk the tutorial, or guess whether a clip rose or fell.

sound.sea_ice: Glass bells. Higher means more ice.
sound.forest: Soft woodwind. Higher means a taller canopy.
sound.precipitation: Rain ticks. Faster means more rain.
sound.co2: Low beating drone. Higher means more carbon dioxide.
sound.aerosols: Hazy pad. Louder means thicker air.
sound.lightning: Sharp cracks. More hits mean more lightning.
sound.events: A short ping for each NASA EONET event, from where it happens.
sound.air_quality: Tight pulse. Higher means dirtier air.
sound.wildfire: Crackle. Louder means a stronger fire.
sound.ocean_sst: Slow swell. Higher means warmer water.
sound.night_lights: Bright chime. Higher means brighter nights.
sound.ocean_currents: A sweep that follows the current.

explain.temperature: Temperature is a warm lead voice. Each note is one year of global temperature since 1880. Higher notes mean a warmer planet.
explain.co2: Carbon dioxide is a low, beating drone. Each pulse is one year measured at Mauna Loa since 1958. As the drone rises, there is more CO2 in the air.
explain.sea_ice: Arctic sea ice sounds like glass bells. Each bell is one September since 1979. Lower bells mean less ice.
explain.wildfire: Wildfires crackle like a marimba. More crackles mean more fire detections. This history is sample data for now.
explain.ocean_sst: Ocean surface temperature comes from NASA's MUR data. Higher notes mean warmer water.
explain.precipitation: Rain comes from NASA's IMERG data. Higher, faster notes mean more rain.
explain.aerosols: Aerosols are dust and smoke in the air. Higher notes mean hazier air.
explain.air_quality: Air quality over Cairo: higher notes mean more fine particles. These values are estimates.
explain.lightning: Lightning is measured from space. More sparks mean more flashes.
explain.forest: Forests are measured by NASA's GEDI laser. Higher notes mean taller trees.
explain.events: Natural events are short signals: storms rumble, fires crackle, volcanoes boom, and ice chimes. Each one plays from where it is happening.
explain.night_lights: Night lights come from NASA's Black Marble images of 2012 and 2016. Higher notes mean brighter nights.
explain.ocean_currents: Ocean currents are flowing lines of sound. This layer is sample data for now.

about.title: About Earth Listens
about.hero: Climate data is mostly pictures. We made it something you can hear.
about.lead: Earth Listens turns real NASA Earth data into music, so blind and low-vision people can explore the planet on their own, by voice and by ear. Sighted visitors get the same data, the same globe and the same guide.
about.how1: We fetch open data from NASA and NOAA: temperature, ice, forests, rain, carbon, air, lightning, fires, oceans and live events.
about.how2: A fixed set of rules turns every number into a note. The same data always makes the same music. No AI makes the sound.
about.how3: An AI guide understands what you say in English or Egyptian Arabic and moves the site for you. It only uses the real numbers on the page.

role.hassan: Team lead · sonification, data, AI guide

about.a11yBody: We aim for WCAG 2.2 AA. Everything works with a keyboard, a screen reader, voice or touch. We never ask about your sight: you choose how to travel, and you can change it any time.
about.challengeBody: Built in 48 hours at NASA Space Apps Cairo, 13–14 November 2026.
about.credits: Data: NASA GISTEMP, NOAA GML, NSIDC, NASA GIBS (MERRA-2, GHRSST MUR, IMERG, GEDI, ISS LIS, AIRS), NASA EONET, NASA FIRMS, NASA GEOS-CF, Open-Meteo, OpenAQ. Imagery: NASA Blue Marble and Black Marble. Voices: Chatterbox by Resemble AI (MIT, watermarked).
